text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-Prime Minister Hariri: We hope to form a government that meets the aspirations of the Lebanese people and tackles crucial social issues.
-French ambassador Lafont: President Chirac highlighted the broad issues that would lead to stability in the region.
-During parliamentary consultations, MPs asked Hariri to form a parliamentary cabinet that tackles social issues, stops corruption and supports the Islamic Resistance.
-German mediators headed by top security official Schmidbauer left to Israel after a long meeting Hizbollah chief Sheikh Nasrallah.
-Lebanon is the victim of an international toxic waste mafia.
-Banque du Liban to own 99 percent of Lebanon's national carrier Middle East Airlines (MEA).
-Israeli troops and their local militia allies on alert inside the zone and troops buildup on the frontlines.
-Maronite Patriarch Sfeir: We still have a long way to democracy and Lebanon must be built on freedom, equality and law.
-Acting Finance Minister Siniora: The consultative committee for the reconstrucion of Lebanon, "Friends of Lebanon", will meet on December 16.
